newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan lawmakers urge delay of CANTV sale.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan lawmakers urge delay of CANTV sale.

text.p: Venezuelan lawmakers from both opposition and government parties said Thursday that the planned sale of the state's 49 percent stake in telephone company CANTV should be delayed until a better price can be obtained.

"It is not in Venezuela's best interest to sell the CANTV shares now, the sale must be postponed," Jorge Roig of the union-based Radical Cause (Causa R) party told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

Roig and other congressmen have said the government should not allow the CANTV sale to go ahead if the expected sale price is below the $4.71 per share obtained for a 40 percent stake of the company in 1991.

Though the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) and investment banks handling the sale of CANTV shares have refused to name a target price, Roig said he had heard the company's shares were being valued at between $2.80 and $3.20 each.

Financial analysts agree that the sale price is very unlikely to match the 1991 price due to the fact that no controlling stake is on offer, CANTV's basic line monopoly has less time to run and prospects for growth are limited.
"We have to suspend the sale now, before the book-building process starts," Roig said.
Roig's position echoed that held by Gustavo Marquez, president of government-supporting Movement to Socialism (MAS) party, who has strongly opposed the sale of CANTV shares at below the 1991 price.
FIV officials could not be reached for comment, but have hinted that they are determined to go ahead with the global issue of 40 percent of CANTV's stock in late November as planned.
Another nine percent is to be offered to employees.
CANTV was partially privatized in 1991 when the VenWorld consortium led by GTE Corp bought a 40 percent stake. Workers bought another 11 percent of the company.

The VenWorld consortium is led by GTE Corp with a 51 percent stake. Local utility Electricidad de Caracas holds 16 percent, Telefnica de Espaa 16 percent, local bank Banco Mercantil BM.CR 12 percent and AT&T five percent.
